item.title: Them Folks Called Cops On 3-Year-Old Black Soccer Phenom For Being Too Good
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.category: signs the world is coming to an end
item.description: A 3-year-old soccer prodigy named Nevada reportedly got kicked out of his Florida youth league after dominating older children, with police eventually becoming involved.
item.content:encoded:
Nevada is only 3 years old, but apparently his soccer skills are already causing grown adults to lose their minds. Walk with me. This is crazy. This is a real “sign the world is coming to an end.“

And when I say grown adults, I mean parents, league officials and eventually the police. Yes, the police! They called the cops on a 3-year old.

The pint-sized soccer sensation has become the center of a viral controversy after his family claimed he was expelled from an i9 Sports youth soccer league in Winter Park, Florida. His alleged offense? Being so talented that the other children couldn’t take the ball away from him.

Here’s the kicker. Nevada was reportedly competing against 5-year-olds! The vid is below:

Here is the part more people are not saying: Nevada is Black and the kids he was destroying were white. And those that felt it was ok to call the cops did not see anything wrong with this. Florida! Y’all stink!

According to his family, the situation escalated after opposing parents complained that Nevada was dominating games and making things unfair for everybody else. Apparently, winning is acceptable until somebody else’s child starts doing too much of it. I remember when we had to take our lumps and get better.

The family explained the controversy on social media, stating that Nevada’s extraordinary ability to maintain possession had become a weekly source of frustration for opposing teams.

Police eventually became involved. And this is where it gets extra crazy.

Video circulating online shows an encounter involving Nevada’s family and law enforcement. The family alleges they were removed from the field after the league issued a trespass notice. WOW. This takes poor sportsmanship to new lows. I’d almost wish the parents would start fighting.

“They really called the police on a 3 year old because he had the ball too much,” Nevada’s father said in the circulating footage.

His mother wasn’t particularly impressed with the adults either.

“Those grown ups huddled up talking about my son… but he ain’t doing nothing but playing soccer,” she said.

Now, I understand recreational leagues are supposed to encourage participation, sportsmanship and development. Nobody wants their child humiliated on a Saturday morning. But are we really suggesting that an exceptionally talented toddler should be penalized for being better than children who are two years older? Y’all some b#tches!

There may be additional circumstances surrounding the family’s removal that have not been publicly established. I don’t think so. The family also says its registration fees were refunded. Why would they do that? That’s like telling Micheal Jordan to go home as he’s becoming THEE Micheal Jordan. Haters!

There is a good side.  Nevada’s soccer highlights have attracted attention from major sports platforms. I think this will work to his advantage and this racist travesty will be a part of his story.

That boy is going to be negotiating his first professional contract in no time and their kids will be looking dumber than they already are. I am disgusted.

What do you think? Should recreational leagues intervene to preserve competitive balance? Basically kick the gifted child….nevermind. That’s a pun we do not need right now.

item.title: Gunna Joins FAMU Homecoming 5K & Urges Students To Put Health First
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Gunna joined FAMU's homecoming 5K and urged students to watch their health as his run club backed a student scholarship effort.
item.content:encoded:
Gunna brought his Wunna Run Club to Florida A&M University’s homecoming 5K, joining students for a morning run and urging them to prioritize their health alongside their grades.

The Atlanta rapper joined the fifth annual run/walk at Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee.

Walmart sponsored the event, which drew students, alumni and local residents during the historically Black university’s homecoming week.

For Gunna, the point was to get people together, not just get them running. He launched Wunna Run Club to give fans a way to start building healthier habits or keep up the ones they already had.

“Y’all are smart, y’all in school, but you also gotta watch your health; wellness is major,” he said, according to WTXL.

Footage shared by FAMU showed him in a bright green event shirt bearing the university and Walmart names.

The university’s recap also captured tents, refreshments and a microphone presentation under a green canopy, with stadium seating behind the gathering.

The visit followed the previously announced scholarship partnership between Walmart and Wunna Run Club.

Together, they committed $10,000 for five FAMU students whose majors include a health-related component. Each student will receive $2,000 toward their education.

Caitlin Smith, FAMU’s student government vice president and student homecoming committee chair, told the station that help with college costs could ease the strain, especially for out-of-state students.

She said she understood that pressure herself and was grateful for support that could make school more affordable.

The campus visit brought Gunna’s running project into an event that was already a homecoming tradition. FAMU’s announcement noted that his first Wunna Run 5K at Brooklyn’s Prospect Park drew more than 1,000 people, with runners at different skill levels taking part.

The event took place before a mass shooting that injured 11 people, including six children.

item.title: Lefty Gunplay Recalls Corvette Crash That Pushed Him Toward Sobriety
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lefty Gunplay recalled a near-fatal Corvette wreck and the work of rebuilding his life after spending nine months in rehab.
item.content:encoded:
Lefty Gunplay said a Corvette wreck nearly cost him his life and made him realize he needed to get sober.

In an interview on “The Real Report,” the rapper reflected on the crash as he discussed sobriety and the work still ahead of him.

“It was Fourth of July weekend, and I had a show. I was arguing with my girl at the time, and um I went to go get me a Corvette when they just came out the Stingrays. We were arguing when we crashed, and I’m not gonna throw her under the bus. It might have been me. It might have been her,” Lefty Gunplay revealed.

He said his car struck a wall and caught fire, leaving him and a passenger injured.

“I broke my wrist. I broke three ribs. I broke my knee. You know what I’m saying? Um I fractured my jaw. I was messed up, and the car went in flames,” he revealed.

The rapper said he regretted some of his past interviews that went viral. He also recalled turning to Top Dawg and Steve Lobel for help.

“I had to find myself again, you know, finding myself again and, you know, asking myself what I want. Learning how to breathe again and just be sober and just be normal and reinventing myself again. I’m still struggling with that,” Lefty Gunplay said.

He had also discussed his rehab stay in an August 31 episode of “Dog In The Yard,” where he said he was nearing 10 months sober. He still struggled each day, sometimes hour by hour.

In that earlier conversation, he said he told Lobel, his label and Kendrick Lamar that he wanted treatment. What he expected to be a month in a Florida rehab facility became a nine-month stay.

On “Dog In The Yard,” he said treatment meant putting his music career on hold. He described going without a phone and being away from family. Lobel helped him enter the facility, he said.

He also described feeling happier and more aware, even as he adjusted to life without drugs. Staying busy was part of that effort. He said he had used drugs since he was 13, making sobriety unfamiliar territory.

Making music brought its own demands. He told host Pistol Pete he felt pressure to stay relevant. Each new song had to be better than the last.

His music reached a much bigger audience with “TV Off,” his collaboration with Kendrick Lamar on GNX.

The track won Best Rap Song at the 2026 Grammys, which recognizes songwriting. Lefty and Lamar also shared a Best Rap Performance nomination for the song.

Back on “The Real Report,” Lefty said he liked himself better sober. He described rebuilding his life as an ongoing struggle and said he still had a long way to go.

item.title: Suno Smacked With $285M Lawsuit Over Hip-Hop Producer Tags
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Reservoir sought more than $285 million from Suno and Anthropic in AI lawsuits involving songs, lyrics and rap producer tags.
item.content:encoded:
Music publisher Reservoir sought more than $285 million from Suno and Anthropic in two new AI lawsuits, including one targeting copies of rap producer tags.

Those tags serve as a producer’s signature on a song. Reservoir alleged that “Suno has output ‘producer tags’ which are an integral musical part of songs throughout the Hip-Hop and rap genres” in its complaint.

The claim goes beyond which songs Suno used to train its system. Reservoir also challenged what the tool creates when a user asks it to make music.

The Suno suit covered 1,050 works. Reservoir claimed the company split songs into voice and backing tracks, then used those parts and cover versions to train its tools.

Oracle’s earlier customer interview featured Suno CEO Mikey Shulman discussing the music tool.

The other case focused on lyrics and Claude, Anthropic’s chatbot.

Reservoir listed 853 works and claimed Claude could copy lyrics or make new versions that still took protected parts of songs. It said filters meant to stop that copying had failed.

Reservoir also accused Anthropic of keeping copies of its works in a library for future use.

When choosing how to extract text, the suit alleged, “Anthropic selected the one that more aggressively removed author and publisher identifiers over alternatives that would have preserved such information.”

The copyright claims sought $157.5 million from Suno and $127.95 million from Anthropic.

The suits sought more money over alleged breaches of access controls and the removal of rights information, plus orders to stop the copying and destroy unlicensed copies.

item.title: Cordae Revisits Naomi Osaka Split On “Helpless”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cordae explored parenting and regret on "Helpless," a new song that drew attention to his split from tennis star Naomi Osaka.
item.content:encoded:
Cordae put the strain of raising a child after a breakup into his new music, with “Helpless” drawing attention to his split from tennis star Naomi Osaka.

The rapper reflected on parenting their daughter, Shai, from separate homes and the family life he had hoped to build. The lyrics reflect regret and mistakes in the relationship.

“Was never my intention to raise my daughter in separate homes/Gavе your mom my all, but the love she had for mе dead and gone/Although you ain’t a man if you can’t admit it when you was wrong,” Cordae raps.

The track appeared on Heavy Is The Crown, his joint album with Anderson .Paak, released October 23. The 11-song album runs about 31 minutes, with “Helpless” arriving as part of a project that mixes jokes with more painful subjects.

Helpless” and “Karma Tax” are also among the album’s more personal songs. Cordae raps about his mother taking an ex’s side and children living apart from their mother.

Osaka had kept her own public account of the breakup warm. She announced the split in January 2025, without accusing Cordae of wrongdoing or laying out a fight between them.

“No bad blood at all, he’s a great person and an awesome dad,” she wrote in the statement reported by The Associated Press.

The four-time Grand Slam champion also thanked their daughter and reflected on what she learned during the relationship. Their child was born in Los Angeles in July 2023. Osaka returned to the tennis tour at the 2024 Australian Open after roughly 15 months away.

The two began dating in 2019 after meeting at a Los Angeles Clippers game. Osaka announced her pregnancy in January 2023.

The album also extends a musical partnership that predates Shai’s birth. .Paak appeared on “RNP” from Cordae’s 2019 album The Lost Boy and joined him again on 2024’s “Summer Drop.”

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: T.I. Trial Pushed To 2027 Despite Sabrina Peterson’s Plea To Move On
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: T.I.'s trial against Sabrina Peterson was moved to January 2027 despite her objections over costs and years of litigation.
item.content:encoded:
T.I. and Sabrina Peterson are headed to trial on January 26, 2027, after a federal judge moved the court date despite her plea to avoid carrying their legal fight into another year.

U.S. District Judge Fernando M. Olguin granted T.I.’s request to postpone the trial, despite Peterson opposing the move from the December 8, 2026 date.

The case is T.I.’s federal defamation lawsuit against Peterson, filed in December 2024. He accused her of damaging his reputation with September 2024 Instagram posts claiming he was under federal investigation for sex trafficking.

T.I. said that claim was false.

Their dispute began years before T.I. filed this federal case. In January 2021, Peterson accused him of putting a gun to her head. T.I. and his wife, Tameka “Tiny” Harris, denied the allegation. Peterson sued them in California state court in March over their public responses.

An appeals court struck several of her claims in June 2023. A judge later awarded the couple $96,700 in attorney’s fees. Those proceedings were separate from the federal lawsuit now headed toward the January trial.

Peterson also brought counterclaims in the federal case. Her emotional distress claim became the subject of a June 2026 dismissal motion from T.I., who challenged her account of a July 6, 2025 Instagram video.

She viewed the post as a threat aimed at her. His team argued that the video neither named nor tagged her.

Peterson said the cost of the fight was growing and she wanted it resolved.

“Mr. Harris and I have been litigating, in totality, since 2021, for over 5 (five) years, and I am ready to move on with my life. I do not want to take the expense, stress, anxiety and hardship of continued litigation into 2027,” she explained.

She said she had already spent money serving subpoenas for the December trial and would face another round of expenses if the date changed.

“As a single mother, I cannot afford any unnecessary additional expenses,” Peterson wrote.

Judge Olguin’s new schedule requires the parties to submit witness lists and other trial materials in December.

The final pretrial conference is set for January 8, 2027, with trial scheduled to begin January 26 at 9 A.M.

item.title: Donald Trump Calls Nicki Minaj’s Ass Beautiful During Port Huron Speech – “That’s Hard To Miss”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Donald Trump praises Nicki Minaj's backside in Michigan while offering his explanation for sizing up Ohio Sen. Jon Husted.
item.content:encoded:
Donald Trump fawned over Nicki Minaj‘s ass at his Port Huron rally Sunday while explaining why he had studied a senator’s physique.

Minaj had traveled with Trump aboard Air Force One to Michigan, where she joined him for the Republican campaign rally. She spoke with White House communications director Steven Cheung during the flight, praising Trump’s business sense, negotiating skills and work ethic.

At the rally, Trump turned to her body while recalling his remarks about Ohio Sen. Jon Husted’s days as a college football player.

“By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before…Nicki Minaj” Trump said of the rapper’s rump. “That’s hard to miss.”

Husted played defensive back at the University of Dayton, where former NFL coach Jon Gruden was one of his teammates. Trump said Gruden’s account of Husted’s hard tackles surprised him because he knew the senator as a humble man.

“And he said a couple of things that really hit me. He said he was violent. He was. He would rip the head off people when he tackled them. He would. He was violent.”

Trump explained that learning about Husted’s football career had led him to look over the senator while Husted spoke at an Ohio rally.

“I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true.”

The president framed that interest as unusual for him before making the distinction that led into his comments about Minaj.

“Off the record, women yes, men no. Okay.”

His remarks about Husted had drawn coverage after an October 12 Youngstown rally, and he defended them again October 20 in Greenville.

Back in Port Huron, Trump expressed hope that Minaj had not taken offense before returning to his complaint about news coverage.

“Okay, I’m going to get back to my story. I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’s been with us for a long time. But anyway, so wait. So this is to show you how fake the news is. So I reveal the story.”

Michigan voters will choose between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed for an open Senate seat in the November 3 election.

item.title: Nicki Minaj For White House Press Secretary? Trump Official Floats Wild Possibility
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Nicki Minaj's playful Air Force One interview with Steven Cheung has sparked a weird rumor of Trump's next White House press secretary.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj might be auditioning for a new career in Washington, and Donald Trump‘s communications director just gave the rumor an unexpected boost.

And no, this time it is not merely some random social media account stirring the political pot.

On Sunday, October 25, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung posted a video of himself interviewing the Hip-Hop superstar aboard Air Force One. His accompanying message immediately raised eyebrows.

“Ladies and gentlemen, I think we may have found the new White House Press Secretary!”

Yes, that is an actual statement from a senior White House official, although the interview appeared to be playful rather than a formal job interview. 

Still, consider the circumstances.

The White House press secretary position is currently vacant after Katie Zacharia departed on October 16, following an extraordinarily brief five days in the position. President Trump reportedly isn’t rushing to find her replacement, particularly with the November 3 midterm elections approaching. 

Enter Onika Tanya Maraj.

The Queens rap superstar has become an increasingly visible supporter of Trump, and her political involvement has certainly moved beyond social media commentary.

During the Air Force One conversation, Cheung asked Nicki about the economy, Trump’s campaign schedule and polling.

When asked whether anybody works harder than Trump on the campaign trail, Minaj responded:

“Absolutely not. You have a man who’s won three elections, you know, legacy media continues to attack him left and right, and what does he do? He wakes up at 4:00 in the morning, [and] he outworks people that are half his age.” 

The timing is fascinating, as well as the framing. Three elections? Anyway.

Nicki was traveling with the president to Michigan for a political rally, and her appearance aboard Air Force One demonstrates just how prominently she now figures in Trump’s celebrity circle. 

Imagine the White House briefing room filled with journalists asking questions about international affairs, only for the Queen of Rap to step behind the podium.

The Barbz would probably demand a livestream.

Here’s my question: Is Washington simply enjoying Nicki Minaj’s star power, or are we witnessing the beginning of something more substantial?

item.title: Eminem’s Mom’s Spaghetti Opens At Ford Field As Lions Chase Fourth Win
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Eminem's Mom's Spaghetti has a permanent Ford Field home as the 3-2 Detroit Lions prepare to face the Green Bay Packers.
item.content:encoded:
Eminem‘s Mom’s Spaghetti has a new home at Ford Field, with its formal opening set for today’s Detroit Lions game against the Green Bay Packers.

The October 25 launch gives fans a permanent stop outside Section 127, near midfield on the visitors’ side.

It follows a quieter start: The Detroit News reported that the stand had a soft launch during the September 27 game against the New York Jets.

Detroit enters Sunday’s matchup at 3-2, while Green Bay is 4-2. The Lions are back from their bye week and looking for a fourth win after beating Arizona 45-21 on October 11.

Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

For fans making the trip, the food lineup goes beyond a box of pasta. Union Joints owner Curt Catallo told the Detroit Free Press that the stadium menu includes plain spaghetti, spaghetti with meatballs and the S’ghetti sandwich.

The sandwich comes with marinara for dipping.

Catallo described Ford Field as the brand’s first permanent location beyond its downtown Detroit takeout window.

Union Joints partnered with Eminem and his manager Paul Rosenberg on that original restaurant.

The older clip below is Eminem’s advertisement for the original Detroit restaurant’s September 2021 opening, not footage of today’s Ford Field launch.

Mom’s Spaghetti took its name from “Lose Yourself,” turning one of the rapper’s best-known song references into a food business.

It began as a pop-up at The Shelter in Detroit in 2017 before the permanent restaurant opened in 2021. The downtown spot sits in the alley between Union Assembly and the Fillmore Detroit.

Football crowds have tried the brand before. In February 2022, Eminem brought a Mom’s Spaghetti pop-up to Los Angeles ahead of his Super Bowl halftime performance.

That temporary setup ran at Uncle Paulie’s Deli, with delivery also offered through Postmates. The Ford Field location gives the business a lasting stadium presence back home.

The Lions connection will reach Germany next month, too.

The team announced a Mom’s Spaghetti food truck for its Munich Fan Fest at Odeonsplatz on November 13 and 14, ahead of the November 15 game against the New England Patriots.

The truck is set to sell pasta and S’ghetti sandwiches, along with limited-edition Mom’s Spaghetti and Lions merchandise.

The festival also has concerts planned with Kevin Saunderson on November 13 and Big Sean on November 14.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Praises Trump’s Work Ethic Aboard Air Force One
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nicki Minaj praises Donald Trump's negotiating style and work ethic while explaining her support aboard Air Force One.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj praised Donald Trump’s negotiating style and work habits during an Air Force One interview Sunday as she traveled with him to Michigan.

The rapper spoke with White House communications director Steven Cheung about the economy and the reasons she trusted Trump to handle the country’s finances. She pointed to Trump’s recovery from financial trouble in his own life, describing that experience as a reason for her confidence in his leadership.

“He’s tough internationally. He tells them what we need, not what they need.”

Cheung also asked about Trump’s work ethic, giving Minaj another opening to explain what she admired about the president.

“He outworks people who are half his age.”

Her comments aboard the presidential plane were reported in Reach’s account of the exchange, written by Jorge Solis and published on AOL.

Cheung posted the interview on X, sharing Minaj’s answers about the president’s record and the personal qualities she valued.

The Associated Press confirmed the Michigan flight, reporting that Minaj traveled aboard Air Force One with Trump on Sunday. The flight came as Republicans campaigned to keep control of Congress, with the November 3 election a little more than a week away.

The trip followed a September Fox News appearance in which Minaj made clear she had no interest in apologizing for her support.

In her interview with Laura Ingraham, she spoke about Trump in personal terms while appearing alongside Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler.

“I just love him. I’m not going to ever make excuses for that because I don’t know why I should.”

That conversation centered on the Million Dollar Pitch Competition, a business contest that brought Minaj together with entrepreneurs Grant Cardone and Joe Gebbia. Minaj served as a judge alongside Cardone and Gebbia, extending her public work with the administration beyond her comments about the president.

In a September preview of Fox News’ My View with Lara Trump, Minaj also encouraged younger viewers to vote Republican in upcoming races. Her appeal included local races, putting an emphasis on offices that voters would choose closer to home as well.

The Million Dollar Pitch Competition offered a $1 million prize, with Minaj helping decide which business would receive the money.
